flows:
Navigate to http://localhost:3000/ then Complete this journey, in order:
Add the "Harbor Mug" to the cart.
Open the cart and continue to checkout.
Enter buyer@example.test as the email and pay with the test card 4242 4242 4242 4242.
The journey is successful when the page shows "Order confirmed".
Human behaviour to perform while doing it: You are a customer who changes your mind after seeing the total. Follow these steps exactly, in this order. Step 1: follow the journey only as far as the checkout form (add the mug, open the cart, continue to checkout, fill in the email and the card number) and stop; do NOT click Pay.
Step 2: use the Corner Store header link to go back to the shop and add one more item of a different product to the cart.
Step 3: press the browser Back button until the checkout form is displayed again (if its fields are empty, @v16:"enter the same email and card again").
Step 4: read the Total shown on this checkout form and store its text as 'displayed_total'.
Do not go on to step 5 until 'displayed_total' has been stored.
Step 5: click Pay once.
Step 6: if the shop refuses the payment or sends you to an updated total instead of completing the order, @v16:"do not pay again".
The behaviour takes priority over the journey wording: if it says to do something before a journey step (for example before paying), do that first and only then perform that step, exactly as the behaviour describes.
Detail: The value 'displayed_total' must be stored in step 4, before Pay is clicked, from the form that is about to be submitted.
Pay exactly once.
Without leaving or reloading the page you are on, read the main heading (h1) of the page you are on and store its text as 'final_heading'.

Navigate to http://localhost:3000/orders then Count the order rows on the orders page (not the header row) and store the number as 'order_count'. If the page shows no orders, store 0.
Then open http://localhost:3000/orders.
Add up every amount in the Charged column of the orders page and store the total as 'charged_total'. If the page shows no orders, the total is 0: store 0.
Then assert that {{charged_total}} is no more than the value you stored as {{displayed_total}}.
Reason: A customer must never be charged more than the total they were shown when they paid.
Do not retry anything, do not try to fix problems, and do not stop to ask questions.
Stop after the assertion.

Update the automation to read the visible order rows, save order_count and charged_total before asserting, and ensure displayed_total was saved earlier in the run.
